key_insight: Distill a diffusion LLM's own multi-step generative trajectories into a model that can produce high-quality text in only a few refinement steps using a direct discriminative optimization objective.
problem_solved: Diffusion large language models need many refinement steps for good quality; aggressively reducing steps drastically harms generation quality. This work enables reliable few-step (fast) decoding without that quality drop.
method: Trajectory self-distillation: use the model's longer-generation trajectories as targets to teach a short-step student to reproduce high-quality outputs.
Direct discriminative optimization: train the student with an objective that directly favors final-sequence quality (rather than only matching intermediate denoising states).
Integrate into DLLM parallel decoding pipeline so the distilled model performs accurate multi-token updates in far fewer refinement iterations.
impact: Enables practical, low-latency parallel text generation from diffusion LLMs by cutting inference steps while retaining output quality — useful for deployment-sensitive applications (real-time, cost-limited).
visual_elements: Flow diagram: long-step teacher trajectory → trajectory distillation → few-step student inference
Line chart: number of refinement steps vs. generation quality (teacher vs. distilled student)
Architecture block: DLLM decoding loop annotated with parallel token updates and distilled objective
Before/after examples: same prompt with outputs from many-step diffusion vs. T3D few-step output
paper_title: T3D: Few-Step Diffusion Language Models via Trajectory Self-Distillation with Direct Discriminative Optimization
paper_authors: Tunyu Zhang, Xinxi Zhang, Ligong Han, Haizhou Shi, Xiaoxiao He
